name: Singleton-Merten Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of dental anomalies including delayed tooth eruption and root dysplasia
Radiographic evidence of aortic and large vessel calcifications
Clinical or laboratory evidence of immune dysregulation such as recurrent infections or autoimmunity
Presence of musculoskeletal abnormalities including osteoporosis or joint contractures
Identification of pathogenic variants in IFIH1 or DDX58 genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (dental anomalies, aortic calcifications, and immune dysregulation) or genetic confirmation with supportive clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis due to phenotypic variability.

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated serum calcium and phosphate
imaging: Calcifications of the ascending aorta and large arteries on CT or X-ray
Dental radiographs showing root hypoplasia and delayed eruption
Osteopenia or osteoporosis on bone densitometry
other: Histopathology of affected tissues showing calcifications and inflammatory infiltrates

distinguishingFeatures: Typically acquired with age or secondary to metabolic disorders

redFlags: Early onset aortic calcifications leading to cardiovascular complications
Severe dental anomalies impairing nutrition and oral health
Recurrent infections or autoimmune manifestations indicating immune dysregulation
references: Singleton-Merten syndrome: clinical and molecular characterization. J Med Genet. 2015.
IFIH1 and DDX58 mutations in Singleton-Merten syndrome. Nat Genet. 2014.
Clinical features and management of Singleton-Merten syndrome. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2017.
